justification: Profile describes the early EP as arrival on indie-pop scene, including electro-laced and intimate material.
Apple Music classifies the original eight-track EP as Indie Rock.
Album-specific genre metadata lists Alternative Rock; Qobuz independently marks Alternative & Indie.
Album-specific tags list Alt-Pop; moderate-confidence platform-level classification.
Album-specific category tags Downtempo; use as a secondary descriptor, not the sole EP genre.
Singer-Songwriter listed as genre; credits identify sombr as sole writer.
Qobuz broad Pop/Rock classification and guitar-led songwriter arrangements; broad umbrella only.
Qobuz release-level Rock classification; broad umbrella, not hard rock.
Apple Music labels the full album Indie Rock; Dork corroborates.
NME describes sad-boy indie and indie pop across the album, with Come Closer as a clear example.
Apple Music describes the record as ornate guitar pop with large arena-ready songs.
AllMusic classifies the album as Alternative/Indie Rock.
Pitchfork discusses bedroom-pop origins developed into modern pop-facing indie; broad alt-pop editorial mapping.
Pitchfork identifies pop instincts, huge choruses and commercial arrangements across the album.
GRAMMY.com describes the album as 1970s-inspired alt-rock with electric guitars.
AllMusic lists contemporary singer/songwriter and discusses his chorus-driven songwriting.
Disco-rock explicitly identified on 12 to 12 only, not the entire record.
MusicRadar calls 12 to 12 a new-wave/disco/synth-pop track.
Explicit 12 to 12 synth-pop style supported by direct breakdown of four-on-floor and Triton.
NME identifies a funk groove on 12 to 12, not a sustained album-wide genre.
NME describes glam-rock qualities of closing song Under the Mat.
NME specifically calls Dime a country-tinged stomper; country is a track accent.
